```markdown
# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md (both Proposed, 2026-10-05; the spec's scope covers O1 only and puts O2–O3 out of scope).
Choices made:
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
- uv workspace with four package scaffolds: sec-edgar-client, sec-edgar-download, sec-edgar-index-ingest, sec-edgar-ingest.
- No platform choice yet: the ADR's Azure decision is Proposed, not accepted.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: ~130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 req/s (SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks of downloading for the full history at 3 req/s (index row count × request rate); not yet measured |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until the submissions are on disk |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression). One track: each outcome consumes the one before it.

## Stages

Order follows your partner's ranking (O1 → O2 → O3), which is also the dependency order. Stages 4–6 are hardening stages for qualities the project needs eventually but not to work. They are placed after the three outcome stages, and the background spec is their main source.

- [ ] Stage 1: Index files into one table (core)
      Objective: Build one filing-index table from real SEC quarterly and daily index files.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a filing-index table built from real quarterly and daily index files; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1: a table holding the rows of real quarterly and daily index files for the range Stage 1 chooses, queryable by CIK, form type and filing date; the findings file records the measured cost of the real run: files and bytes downloaded, rows loaded, elapsed time and the request rate achieved.
      Leaves out: raw-snapshot retention and replay → Stage 4; versioned publication manifest → Stage 4; row provenance → Stage 4; historical-format fixture suite → Stage 4; quarterly reconciliation and withdrawals → Stage 5; scheduled daily runs and catch-up → Stage 6; shared request budget across concurrent runs → Stage 6; monitoring and alerts → Stage 6; cloud deployment → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions download
      Objective: Download the submissions that the Stage 1 table's rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: submissions on disk, each one locatable from its index row
      Exit: O2: for the range Stage 2 chooses, every index row maps to a downloaded submission or a listed failure, and the measured download rate is recorded.
      Leaves out: download manifest and checksums → Stage 4; scheduled download of new submissions → Stage 6; shared request budget across concurrent runs → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table; Stage 2's submissions on disk
      Produces: extracted main documents for the 10-K and 8-K filings in the downloaded range
      Exit: O3: every 10-K and 8-K in the downloaded range has an extracted main document or a listed failure with its reason.
      Leaves out: extraction provenance → Stage 4; scheduled extraction of new filings → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests, replay and traceability
      Objective: Bring O1–O3 to final standard for retained inputs, versioned publication and provenance.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 outputs
      Produces: raw-snapshot retention and replay; versioned publication manifest; row provenance; download manifest and checksums; extraction provenance; historical-format fixture suite
      Exit: O1: a parser change rebuilds the table from retained raw index files without SEC requests, and readers resolve a versioned manifest. O2: every downloaded submission has a manifest entry with its checksum. O3: every extracted document traces to its submission and extractor version.
      Leaves out: quarterly reconciliation and withdrawals → Stage 5; scheduled operation → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Quarterly reconciliation
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and account for additions, changed fields and withdrawals without discarding history.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 4's raw-snapshot retention and replay and versioned publication manifest
      Produces: quarterly reconciliation and withdrawals
      Exit: O1: a re-read of the quarterly indexes publishes additions and field changes as a new version, and any removal of keys waits for recorded approval.
      Leaves out: scheduled reconciliation runs → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Scheduled operation and deployment
      Objective: Run index ingestion, submission download, extraction and reconciliation on a schedule in a deployed environment.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–5 outputs
      Produces: scheduled daily runs and catch-up; scheduled download of new submissions; scheduled extraction of new filings; scheduled reconciliation runs; shared request budget across concurrent runs; monitoring and alerts; cloud deployment
      Exit: O1: scheduled daily runs ingest new index files and catch up after a missed run. O2: new submissions download on schedule within one shared SEC request budget. O3: new 10-K and 8-K filings are extracted on schedule. Alerts fire on failed runs, and each observed scheduled run has a durable report.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run derive-roadmap §6 over the Outcomes list (O1–O3). Give evidence per verdict: the implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, and deferred_items entries. Each unmet outcome exits as a new stage or as a conscious deferral with a written why. Then retire this file to `specs/completed/`.
```
